websiteToolPlateCalculator.title: Plate calculator
websiteToolPlateCalculator.intro: Enter the weight you want on the bar and get the plates for each side, using the plates your gym actually has, in kg or lb, with your own bar.

form.targetHint: The total on the bar, bar included.

problems.target: Enter the target weight as a number above 0 and at most {{max}} {{unit}}.

results.exact: Your gym can load this weight exactly.
results.inexact: Your gym cannot make {{target}} exactly. The heaviest it can load is {{below}}, and the nearest loadable weight is {{nearest}}.
results.belowBar: That is lighter than the bar ({{bar}}). Pick a heavier target, or set a lighter bar in your gym.
results.noPlates: No plates are needed: the bar alone is the target.
results.barLine: Bar: {{bar}}. Plates are loaded in pairs, one on each side.

sections.title: Why the heaviest plate first is wrong
body: The usual method takes the heaviest plate that fits, then the next, and so on. That works when a gym has plenty of every plate. With limited plates it can fail: a gym with one pair each of 20, 15 and 10 kg needs 25 kg a side for a load of 70 kg with a 20 kg bar. Taking the 20 first leaves 5 kg that no plate fills. The answer is 15 and 10 kg, which the gym can load.
This calculator tries the combinations of the plates you enter and picks the heaviest load that does not go over your target, using the fewest plates.

sections.title: Plates load in pairs
body: A bar takes plates in pairs, one on each side, so each plate you enter counts as pairs. An odd plate in a gym cannot be used for a pair and is left out. Enter how many pairs of each plate you have.

sections.title: Bar weight and units
body: The bar is part of the total, so set your bar's weight first. Standard Olympic bars are 20 kg (45 lb), and some are lighter. Type in kg or lb: the app stores kilograms and converts, so the numbers match the Musclog app.
